title: architecture-review-kv-cache-splitter-concurrency-2026-06-02
content:
Attendees: Aisha Patel (chair), Marcus Lee, Sofia Martinez, Ravi Kapoor, Emily Chen, Jordan Wu (notes)
Date: 2026-06-02
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime
Duration: 60m

Goal:
- Review the KV-cache splitter concurrency model (follow-up to prior splitter design) and agree on safe defaults and rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted.

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of splitter goals and prior decisions (5m)
2) Concurrency model: per-route vs global token budget (15m)
3) Eviction & backpressure interactions under high-concurrency (15m)
4) Canary/rollout plan + telemetry knobs (15m)
5) Action items & owners (10m)

Recap:
- Splitter responsibility: maintain prefix/KV caches per-route and route requests to appropriate backend/model variants while keeping KV cache locality and avoiding hot-shard contention. Prior RFC decided on logical splitters per-tenant and optional multi-tenant pooled splitters for low-volume tenants.

Discussion notes:
- Concurrency models considered:
  * Per-route concurrency limit: token-based budget assigned per logical route. Simple to reason about but can underutilize pooled GPU capacity when one route is idle.
  * Global pool with weighted shares: routes get weighted shares of a global budget, allows smoothing but adds complexity in fairness and accounting.
  * Hybrid: per-route soft limits with global overflow (burst) window. This reduces risk of noisy-neighboring routes exhausting global capacity.

- Safety & predictable latency: We need a model that prevents cache thrash and prevents eviction storms when many routes simultaneously increase traffic. Participants prefer the hybrid model as default.

- Implementation constraints:
  * Need deterministic admission and a simple counter for in-flight token usage to keep cross-language surface minimal.
  * Avoid heavy coordination on the critical path—use local estimators + occasional sync to central controller for weights.
  * For Dedicated, allow operator overrides (static tenant commitment) that pin larger soft limits.

- Eviction & backpressure interactions:
  * Eviction should be rate-limited and driven by a score that combines last-access, route priority, and write amplification cost.
  * Under high concurrency, we must avoid cascading evictions across many shards. Proposal: introduce 'eviction windows' where eviction budget is limited per time window per splitter instance.
  * Backpressure policy: when admission denied, prefer queueing (bounded wait) for low-latency routes and immediate fallback for best-effort batch routes.

- Telemetry & observability needs:
  * Metrics: per-route in_flight_tokens, queue_length, eviction_count, eviction_window_exhausted, admission_denials, fallback_count, token_wait_latency p50/p95/p99.
  * Traces: tag traces when admission was denied and when fallback model used.
  * Dashboards: canary dashboard showing eviction_rate and latency by route during rollout.

- Rollout & canary plan:
  1) Implement hybrid admission controller behind feature flag. Unit tests + load test harness to simulate 1k concurrent routes.
  2) Internal canary: enable for eng-serving-runtime routes with synthetic load for 48h, monitor eviction and P95 latency.
  3) Gradual enablement on Hosted default for new routes behind opt-in; enable for Dedicated customers only after ops sign-off.
  4) Provide runtime knobs: global_token_budget, per_route_soft_limit, overflow_window_size, eviction_budget_per_window. Default conservative values chosen to avoid customer impact.

- Performance testing notes:
  * Load test scenarios should include: many low-qps routes, few high-qps routes, and mixed bursts.
  * Validate KV cache hit rate delta and model P95 latency under each scenario.

Decisions made:
- Adopt hybrid concurrency model (per-route soft limits + small global overflow window) as default.
- Implement eviction windows to rate-limit evictions during spikes.
- Default rollout: feature-flagged implementation -> eng canary -> opt-in Hosted -> Dedicated with ops approval.
- Telemetry set defined (see above) must be emitted at GA.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Exact default numeric values for budgets and window sizes (TBD after load testing).
- How to expose per-route overrides in the public API without overwhelming users with knobs. Proposal: expose presets (low, medium, high) + advanced config for Dedicated customers.

Action items:
- Aisha: Draft feature PR skeleton and config schema (due 2026-06-08).
- Marcus: Implement admission controller POC and local estimator (due 2026-06-15).
- Sofia: Extend load test harness to simulate mixed-burst scenarios and run baseline tests (due 2026-06-10).
- Ravi: Design eviction scoring function and implement eviction window enforcement in simulator (due 2026-06-12).
- Emily: Dashboard templates + alert thresholds for canary (due 2026-06-14).
- Jordan: Update linked RFCs and add test cases to RFC-142 doc (due 2026-06-09).

Notes for follow-up meeting:
- Bring initial numbers from load tests to pick concrete defaults.
- Review canary results and decide rollout timing for Hosted.

Appendix / references:
- See RFC-142-kv-cache-sharding for baseline assumptions.
- GH: redwood/runtime#3587 contains POC code for admission counters.
- JIRA SRV-2241 tracks the eviction workstream.

Meeting closed 60m.
